besanosaurus:enwiki:7.title: Besanosaurus (Putative specimens from Svalbard and Germany, part 2)

facts.statement: The genus Besanosaurus was named by Dal Sasso and Pinna in 1996.
facts.quote: authority: Dal Sasso & Pinna, 1996

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Besanosaurus is the nearly complete flattened skeleton designated BES SC 999.
facts.quote: Besanosaurus was named by Cristiano Dal Sasso and Giovanni Pinna in 1996, based on the nearly complete flattened skeleton BES SC 999, the holotype specimen.

facts.statement: Specimens previously classified as the genus Mikadocephalus have been reinterpreted as belonging to Besanosaurus.
facts.quote: Additional specimens from Monte San Giorgio that have previously been considered separate genera, including a partial skull named Mikadocephalus and a well-preserved, largely complete skeleton, have been reinterpreted as additional specimens of Besanosaurus.

facts.statement: Putative specimens of Besanosaurus have been found in Svalbard and Germany, but their classification is disputed.
facts.quote: Putative specimens have been discovered in the Norwegian archipelago of Svalbard and Germany, although their attribution to the genus remains disputed.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic, specifically the latest Anisian stage.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Middle Triassic, latest Anisian,

facts.statement: Besanosaurus fossils are found in Monte San Giorgio, a region spanning Italy and Switzerland.
facts.quote: Besanosaurus (meaning reptile from Besano) is an extinct genus of Middle Triassic ichthyosaur from Monte San Giorgio of Italy and Switzerland

facts.statement: All confirmed specimens of Besanosaurus originate from the Besano Formation.
facts.quote: All definite specimens of Besanosaurus come from the Besano Formation.

facts.statement: During the Anisian, the Besano Formation represented a lagoon inhabited by diverse marine life including other ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: During the Anisian, this region was a lagoon populated by a wide variety of marine life, including a variety of other ichthyosaurs.

facts.statement: The largest known specimen of Besanosaurus is estimated to be about 8 meters long.
facts.quote: Besanosaurus is a large ichthyosaur, with the largest known specimen estimated to measure about 8 m long.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus possessed a long, thin snout containing numerous small, pointed teeth.
facts.quote: The snout of Besanosaurus is long and thin, and contains numerous small pointed teeth.

facts.statement: The tail of Besanosaurus made up more than half of the animal's total length and had a downward bend.
facts.quote: The tail made up more than half the animal's length and displays a downward bend.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus had forelimbs longer than its hindlimbs, with round and squat humeri.
facts.quote: The forelimbs are longer than the hindlimbs, and the humeri are round and squat.

facts.statement: It is unclear how Besanosaurus is exactly related to other members of the shastasaurid group.
facts.quote: While it is understood to be a shastasaurid-type ichthyosaur, how exactly Besanosaurus and other members of this group are related to each other is unclear.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Besanosaurus had strong jaw muscles and fed on small fish and coleoid cephalopods using rapid snapping bites.
facts.quote: The skull bones of Besanosaurus indicate that it would have possessed strong jaw muscles, but its delicate snout suggests it would have fed on small fish and coleoid cephalopods, which it could have caught with rapid, snapping bites.

facts.statement: Mikadocephalus gracilirostris is a synonym of Besanosaurus leptorhynchus.
facts.quote: synonyms: * Mikadocephalus gracilirostris Maisch & Matzke, 1997

facts.statement: By February 1996, approximately 2500 hours of preparation had been performed on the Besanosaurus holotype.
facts.quote: By February 1996, 2500 hours of preparation had been performed by three or four preparators on the specimen, exposing the skull and appendicular skeleton.

facts.statement: It took a total of 16,500 hours over 5 years to fully prepare the skeleton, which was hidden under 21,000 cm² of rock.
facts.quote: It ultimately took 16500 hours spread over 5 years in total to fully reveal the skeleton, which was concealed under 21000 cm2 of rock.

facts.statement: Some researchers have debated whether Besanosaurus might actually be another specimen of the genus Shastasaurus.
facts.quote: While P. Martin Sander and Christiane Faber in 1998 considered it possible that Besanosaurus represented another specimen of the related Shastasaurus, Besanosaurus has otherwise been accepted as a valid taxon.

facts.statement: The holotype of Besanosaurus was not the first shastasaurid specimen discovered in Monte San Giorgio.
facts.quote: The holotype of Besanosaurus was not the first shastasaur known from Monte San Giorgio.

facts.statement: Two shastasaurid specimens from Switzerland were deposited in the collections of the Paläontologisches Institut und Museum der Universität Zürich in the 1920s.
facts.quote: Two shastasaurid specimens from Switzerland were deposited in the collections of Paläontologisches Institut und Museum der Universität Zürich in the 1920s

facts.statement: Specimen PIMUZ T 4847, recovered from layer 116 of the Cava Tre Fontane mine, is very large, poorly preserved, disarticulated, and missing the tail and limbs.
facts.quote: The other specimen, hailing from layer 116 of the Cava Tre Fontane mine, is cataloged as PIMUZ T 4847 and is very large, and poorly preserved and disarticulated, missing the tail and limbs.

facts.statement: In 1997, Michael Maisch and Andreas Matzke described an ichthyosaur skull cataloged as GPIT 1793/1 housed at the Palaeontological Collection of Tübingen University.
facts.quote: In 1997, Michael Maisch and Andreas Matzke described an ichthyosaur skull housed at the Palaeontological Collection of Tübingen University, cataloged as GPIT 1793/1.

facts.statement: Sander considered it possible that Wimanius was a juvenile Besanosaurus rather than a distinct genus.
facts.quote: He also considered it possible that Wimanius, another fragmentary ichthyosaur named in 1998 by Maisch and Matzke, was a juvenile Besanosaurus rather than its own genus

facts.statement: Sander argued that better-preserved material needed to be studied before definite taxonomic assignments could be made.
facts.quote: However, Sander argued that the better-preserved material would need to be studied before definite assignments could be made.

facts.statement: McGowan and Motani considered both Mikadocephalus and Wimanius potentially synonymous with Pessosaurus, though they remained tentative because the material was not studied firsthand.
facts.quote: They considered both genera potentially synonymous with the much earlier-named Pessosaurus, though remained tentative as the material was not studied firsthand.

facts.statement: In 2021, Gabriele Bindellini and colleagues published a paper detailing the skull anatomy of Besanosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2021, a paper by Gabriele Bindellini and colleagues detailing the skull anatomy of Besanosaurus was published.

facts.statement: Bindellini and colleagues reassessed Mikadocephalus, finding that features used to distinguish it were also present in Besanosaurus and no distinguishing characteristics could be found between the two genera.
facts.quote: The authors reassessed the status of Mikadocephalus, finding many of the features initially used to distinguish it to be present in Besanosaurus as well, and were not able to find any distinguishing characteristics between the two genera.

facts.statement: Bindellini and colleagues synonymized Mikadocephalus gracilirostris with Besanosaurus leptorhynchus and referred four other specimens to B. leptorhynchus.
facts.quote: Therefore, they synonymized M. gracilirostris with B. leptorhynchus, and referred the other four specimens to the latter species as well

facts.statement: The first remains of Besanosaurus consisted of 11 vertebrae and some rib fragments discovered in the 1860s.
facts.quote: The first remains of this taxon were a total of 11 vertebrae with some associated rib fragments found during the 1860s

facts.statement: John Hulke named the initial remains Ichthyosaurus polaris in 1873.
facts.quote: named Ichthyosaurus polaris by John Hulke in 1873

facts.statement: Carl Wiman established the genus Pessosaurus to contain the species formerly known as Ichthyosaurus polaris.
facts.quote: Carl Wiman named a new genus, Pessosaurus, to contain the species

facts.statement: Bindellini and colleagues concluded in 2024 that there is no evidence of Besanosaurus from Svalbard.
facts.quote: Bindellini and colleagues in 2024 also considered Pessopteryx to be distinct from Besanosaurus, and concluded that there was no evidence of Besanosaurus from Svalbard

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene erected the species Pessosaurus suevicus in 1916 based on a single vertebra found in the Black Forest, Germany.
facts.quote: In 1916, Friedrich von Huene erected a second species of Pessosaurus, P. suevicus, on the basis of a single vertebra discovered in the Muschelkalk of the Black Forest in the state of Baden-Württemberg, Germany

facts.statement: Maisch and Matzke noted in 2000 that the fossil material of P. suevicus might come from Besanosaurus but agreed it could not be distinguished from other group representatives.
facts.quote: Maisch and Matzke noted in 2000 the possibility that the fossil material came from Besanosaurus or a similar ichthyosaur, but agreed that it could not be distinguished from other representatives of the group

facts.statement: Besanosaurus is more elongate than later ichthyosaurs and resembles Cymbospondylus in overall shape.
facts.quote: Besanosaurus is more elongate, and resembles Cymbospondylus in overall shape

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Besanosaurus measures 5.065 meters long from snout to tail tip.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen measures 5.065 m long from its snout tip to tail tip

facts.statement: The specimen PIMUZ T 4847 was estimated to be 8 meters long in 2021 and is the largest known specimen of Besanosaurus.
facts.quote: The specimen PIMUZ T 4847 was estimated by Bindellini and colleagues in 2021 to have a total length of 8 m, and is the largest known specimen of Besanosaurus

facts.statement: Approximately two-thirds of the Besanosaurus skull is occupied by a long, thin snout lined with small teeth.
facts.quote: About two-thirds of the skull of Besanosaurus is occupied by its very long, thin snout lined with small teeth.

facts.statement: Well-preserved skulls of Besanosaurus feature drawn-out, slot-like external nares that housed the nostrils.
facts.quote: Well-preserved Besanosaurus skulls show drawn-out slotlike external nares, openings which housed the nostrils in life.

facts.statement: Bindellini and colleagues estimated that Besanosaurus had between 15 and 17 scleral ring plates per ring.
facts.quote: Bindellini and colleagues estimated a total of between 15 and 17 of these plates per ring in Besanosaurus.

facts.statement: The region behind the orbits of Besanosaurus occupies 13% of the skull's length, which is longer than in some parvipelvian ichthyosaurs.
facts.quote: The region behind the orbits is short, occupying 13% of the skull's length, though it is still long compared to some parvipelvians.

facts.statement: The jugal bones of Besanosaurus are thin, strip-like structures bent at right angles.
facts.quote: The jugals are thin, strip-like bones bent at right angles.

facts.statement: The stapes bones in the Besanosaurus braincase are broad-ended but have slender shafts.
facts.quote: The stapedes of Besanosaurus, a pair of bones in the braincase, are broad-ended but slender-shafted.

facts.statement: Most of the Besanosaurus lower jaw is formed by long, thin dentaries that bear teeth.
facts.quote: Most of the lower jaw is formed by the long, thin toothbearing dentaries.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus tooth crowns have vertical ridges without cutting edges, while the roots possess even stronger ridging.
facts.quote: The tooth crowns are lined with vertical ridges, though lack cutting edges, while the tooth roots bear even stronger ridging.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus teeth are widely spaced and interlock when the jaw is closed.
facts.quote: The teeth are separated from each other by a rather wide amount of space and interlock when the jaw is closed.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the kidney-shaped quadrates with a triangular eminence are unique to Mikadocephalus or a widespread feature of shastasaurids, with recent evidence suggesting the latter.
facts.quote: In 1997, Maisch and Matzke considered this to be a unique feature of Mikadocephalus, as at the time it was only known in the holotype skull of that taxon; however, Bindellini and colleagues identified this on multiple Besanosaurus specimens in 2021, as well as a specimen of Guanlingsaurus, and therefore suggested that it may be a fairly widespread feature of shastasaurids.

facts.statement: The fossil bones of Besanosaurus were first discovered in the "Sasso Caldo" quarry in the spring of 1993.
facts.quote: Los huesos fósiles del Besanosaurus fueron descubiertos por primera vez en el cantera "Sasso Caldo" en la primavera de 1993

facts.statement: The Besanosaurus skeleton was prepared in the paleontological laboratory of the Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Milano after 16,500 hours of work.
facts.quote: El esqueleto de Besanosaurus salió a la luz en el laboratorio paleontológico del Museo Civico di Storia Naturale di Milano después de 16.500 horas de preparación.

facts.statement: 145 X-rays were required to detect the contents of the 38 stone slabs containing the skeleton.
facts.quote: para detectar el contenido de las 38 losas de piedra en las que se distribuía el esqueleto, hicieron falta 145 radiografías.

facts.statement: The 38 stone slabs were reassembled and a silicone rubber matrix was created to produce a mold of the original specimen.
facts.quote: Las 38 losas fueron re-ensambladas y una matriz de goma de silicona fue hecha, con lo que se obtuvo un molde del espécimen original.

facts.statement: The holotype of Besanosaurus preserves 201 vertebrae, with 61 located anterior to the hips.
facts.quote: The holotype of Besanosaurus preserves 201 vertebrae, 61 of which are located in front of the hips.

facts.statement: The tail of the holotype constitutes more than half of the animal's total length and contains at least 138 vertebrae.
facts.quote: The tail of the holotype makes up more than half of the animal's length and contains at least 138 vertebrae.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus was a reptile approximately 6 meters in length.
facts.quote: Besanosaurus era un reptil de cerca de 6 metros de longitud

facts.statement: Besanosaurus had a slender snout, small teeth, lacked a dorsal fin, and possessed a long, slender tail.
facts.quote: Tenía un hocico delgado, algunos dientes pequeños, carecía de aleta dorsal y poseía una cola larga y delgada.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus likely swam by undulating its body like an eel, suggesting modest speed but capable of rapid acceleration and good maneuverability.
facts.quote: Parece haber sido un nadador que ondulaba su cuerpo de manera similar a una anguila, de modo que debió tener una modesta velocidad pero era capaz de una rápida aceleración y buena maniobrabilidad

facts.statement: Besanosaurus was a carnivore that primarily ate small fish, cephalopods, and other marine reptiles.
facts.quote: Besanosaurs era un carnívoro que comía mayormente peces pequeños, cefalópodos y otros reptiles marinos.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus was likely ovoviviparous, meaning eggs incubated inside the body and young were born developed.
facts.quote: Probablemente era de reproducción ovovivípara, lo que significa que los huevos se incubaban dentro del cuerpo y así nacían ya desarrollados.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus lived during the Middle Triassic period, approximately 235 million years ago.
facts.quote: que vivió durante el periodo Triásico Medio, hace aproximadamente 235 millones de años.

facts.statement: Besanosaurus inhabited tropical coastal seas similar to the current Caribbean Sea.
facts.quote: ideales para su hábitat de mares tropicales costeros, similares al actual Mar Caribe.

facts.statement: The parent group of Besanosaurus is Besanosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Besanosauridae
